articles.title: Centre Party flips: Board and MPs ready to back Kristersson as Swedish PM
articles.summary: After a meeting lasting several hours, Centre Party representatives on Thursday urged the party to vote yes to Ulf Kristersson as prime minister, leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist announced at a late-afternoon press conference.

articles.title: Internal rebellion brews in Sweden's Centre Party over potential centre-right coalition
articles.summary: An increasing number of voices are calling for the Centre Party to go into opposition rather than joining a centre-right government dependent on the Sweden Democrats.

articles.title: Insider source stories split on Swedish Centre Party's emergency meeting
articles.summary: The Centre Party, a kingmaker in Sweden's ongoing government negotiations, held an emergency meeting late Tuesday night. But what happened in it? Party sources are telling different stories to different media outlets.

articles.title: Swedish MPs set to vote on Ulf Kristersson as right-wing PM on Monday
articles.summary: Sweden's parliament will vote whether to give Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson a new four-year mandate on November 30th after inconclusive elections.

articles.title: 'Time to fight': Swedish Centre Party councillor blasts move for Kristersson deal
articles.summary: Christian Widlund, a city councillor for the Centre Party, who is one of the most outspoken opponents of his party being in a government dependent on the far-right Sweden Democrats, has told The Local there will be "uproar" if party backs Ulf Kristersson as PM.

articles.title: Sweden's Moderate leader Ulf Kristersson 'prepared' to face prime ministerial vote
articles.summary: Moderate Party Ulf Kristersson has informed the speaker of parliament that he is ready for a vote on becoming prime minister.

articles.title: OPINION: Sweden's red-green parties are on the brink of a historic betrayal
articles.summary: More than 100,000 citizenship applicants were given reason to believe that Sweden would restore its commitment to fairness and the rule of law. That hope now risks becoming collateral damage in a shameful struggle for political power, writes Patrick Gallen, spokesperson for the Fair Transition campaign.

articles.title: Sweden's Centre Party to start talks to form right-wing government
articles.summary: Sweden's Centre Party has announced that it will now restart negotiations on backing Moderate Party leader Ulf Kristersson, after failing to reach agreement with the Left Party.

articles.title: Swedish parties pledge citizenship transition rules in final offer to Left Party
articles.summary: The Social Democrats, Green Party and Centre Party have agreed to bring back transitional rules for citizenship in one of the 18 policy proposals offered to the Left Party as part of the price for backing Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson as prime minister.

articles.title: EXPLAINED: What was in the 'last chance' offer to Sweden's Left Party?
articles.summary: In a 'starter pack', the Social Democrats, Green Party and Centre Party offered the Left Party a place in an inner cabinet, 18 policy proposals including an end to unfair deportations, transitional provisions for citizenship... and an apology.

articles.title: Centre Party districts open to talks on forming right-wing Swedish government
articles.summary: Centre Party heavyweights have said they are open to negotiations over a right-wing government after the party's deputy leader gave the Left Party one day to accept a final offer.

articles.title: EU proposes tax on Big Tech to boost budget
articles.summary: The EU put forward plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to fund its next budget Saturday, as it seeks to bridge divisions among member states over the bloc's long-term funding.

articles.title: 'Shameful': Swedish citizenship applicants outraged by 'pairing' deal
articles.summary: Sweden's parliamentary leaders have agreed on a new 'pairing' agreement to allow MPs to be absent for votes without changing the chamber balance. But for those who were caught in the crossfire of the previous agreement's collapse, the most important element is missing.

articles.title: Sweden's Centre and Left parties blame each other as round-the-clock talks end in deadlock
articles.summary: Negotiations between Sweden's so-called 'red-green' parties remained deadlocked on Friday afternoon, as the four parties continued talks on forming a new government under tight time constraints at an undisclosed location.

articles.title: Master stroke or dead end? The high-stakes gamble of Sweden's Centre Party
articles.summary: Attempts by Swedish politicians to form a government have been going on for two months, without any sign yet of a breakthrough. “The Centre Party is playing for very high stakes indeed,” says political scientist Nicholas Aylott.

articles.title: ANALYSIS: Eight reasons why Sweden's Left Party is stubbornly sticking to its guns
articles.summary: Why, you might wonder, is Sweden's Left Party so determined to get a ministerial position in the next government that it seems willing to risk a new election or even another four years of right-wing rule? Well, here's why.

articles.title: Church chapter pauses investigation into Swedish PM's wife
articles.summary: The Chapter of the Diocese of Strängnäs is pausing its investigation into whether Birgitta Ed, the wife of acting Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, is suitable to serve as a priest after questions surfaced about volunteers for her foundation receiving plum government jobs.

articles.title: Sweden's Moderates overtake Social Democrats for first time in ten years
articles.summary: The right-wing Moderate Party has scored higher than the Social Democrats in an opinion poll for the first time in more than ten years as voters tire of the long wait to agree on a government.

articles.title: Swedish parliament agrees on new 'pairing' agreement after citizenship vote breakdown
articles.summary: Six months after the previous agreement collapsed, causing chaos in Sweden's parliament, parliamentary leaders have finally agreed on a new 'pairing' agreement to allow MPs to be absent for votes without changing the chamber balance.

articles.title: Social Democrats offer work permit overhaul in 135-point pitch to Centre Party
articles.summary: The Social Democrats have promised the Centre Party to scrap the restrictive work permit rules brought in by the Tidö government and bring an end to 'talent deportations' as part of a new 'strict but reasonable migration policy'.

articles.title: Swedish parties pledge citizenship transition rules in final offer to Left Party
articles.summary: The Social Democrats, Green Party and Centre Party have agreed to bring back transitional rules for citizenship in one of the 18 policy proposals offered to the Left Party as part of the price for backing Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson as prime minister.

articles.title: 'No idea why': Foreigners in Sweden face investigations into revoking permanent residency
articles.summary: More and more foreigners in Sweden are being sent letters from the Migration Agency warning that their permanent residence permits could be revoked. We spoke to some of them and asked lawyers and the Migration Agency why this is happening.

articles.title: Swedish Migration Agency rolls out new logo with coat of arms
articles.summary: Wondering where that red arc went? The Swedish Migration Agency's old logo is history, as it moves to put its new logo, featuring the agency's connection to the Swedish state, in more places.

articles.title: EXPLAINED: Who could lose Swedish citizenship after new constitution changes?
articles.summary: The Swedish parliament voted to amend Sweden's constitution to enable authorities to strip dual citizens of their Swedish citizenship in certain situations. Do we know what they are?

articles.title: Social Democrats offer work permit overhaul in 135-point pitch to Centre Party
articles.summary: The Social Democrats have promised the Centre Party to scrap the restrictive work permit rules brought in by the Tidö government and bring an end to 'talent deportations' as part of a new 'strict but reasonable migration policy'.

articles.title: How integration policies are becoming more stringent across Europe
articles.summary: Citizenship policy is increasingly used by governments in rich countries to define migrants’ “integration expectations,” according to a landmark report on international migration.

articles.title: EXPLAINED: When do you have to leave Sweden to change permit type?
articles.summary: The Local has reported on several cases recently where foreigners have been forced to leave Sweden to apply for a residency permit on new grounds. Here are the rules to the best of our understanding.

articles.title: Blame game over dwindling chance to stop Sweden's unfair deportations
articles.summary: A bitter blame game has erupted between leading Left Party and Centre Party MPs, with each accusing the other of squandering a chance to stop unfair deportations by blocking a Magdalena Andersson government.

articles.title: Sweden changes constitution to allow revoking citizenship of dual nationals
articles.summary: Sweden's parliament has approved a constitutional change to allow the citizenship of dual nationals to be revoked if they obtained it fraudulently or were convicted of crimes threatening national interests.

articles.title: Parliament to vote on revoking citizenship for 'crimes that harm Sweden's vital interests'
articles.summary: Sweden's parliament is set to vote on Wednesday to change the constitution to make it possible for dual citizens convicted of 'crimes that seriously harm Sweden's vital interests' to be stripped of their Swedish citizenship.

articles.title: Why is it taking five years to develop language tests for Swedish citizenship?
articles.summary: Eighteen months after Stockholm University was instructed to develop language tests for citizenship, it has finally hired a project manager. Lars Bokander told The Local that when it comes to developing test items, he is "more or less starting from scratch".

articles.title: Sweden Democrat leader backs 'open Swedishness' amid high-profile party clash
articles.summary: Sweden Democrat leader Jimmie Åkesson has waded into an ongoing internal party row over what defines Swedish identity.

articles.title: What would it take for Swedish Migration Agency to freeze 'teen deportations'?
articles.summary: The Swedish Migration Agency will not freeze the controversial deportations of young adults – yet.

articles.title: 'He's the reason I'm here': Dad fights to stay in Sweden with baby son
articles.summary: A committed father was left 'speechless' by a Swedish Migration Court decision saying moving to 'visa-free visits' from the UK would not unduly affect his relationship with his one-year-old son. He is fighting the deportation order with a second appeal.

articles.title: Inside Sweden: Why force foreigners to leave Sweden to change their residency permit?
articles.summary: Richard Orange suggests that Sweden should stop splitting couples and families by forcing people to leave Sweden when applying for residency on new grounds, before running through the week's news.

articles.title: Sweden's centre-left bloc agrees on plan to halt teen deportations
articles.summary: Sweden's centre-left parties have reached an agreement on how to draft a emergency law halting so-called "teenage deportations".

articles.title: How did Swedish media cover the 'migration paradigm shift'?
articles.summary: Immigration was at the heart of the political debate in the past four years, but the voices of immigrants themselves were comparatively rarely centred in the media coverage, an analysis by The Fix Research & Advisory in partnership with The Local shows.

articles.title: 'I want to be with my husband': Pregnant woman forced to leave Sweden
articles.summary: Newly married and expecting her first child, it should be the happiest year of Brenda Ramström's life. But today she's going to have to get on a flight back home to Brazil, not knowing when she'll be able to reunite with her husband in Sweden.

articles.title: Foreign SSAB workers released as Dutch lawyer slams Swedish site raid
articles.summary: The 19 Filipino electrical engineers who were seized by Swedish police on October 9th and held in a Migration Agency detention centre have been released, with the company's lawyer calling the decision to detain them "unlawful" and promising to seek damages.

articles.title: Tech leader wins appeal under Sweden's new citizenship rules
articles.summary: The AI consultant Anna Bärlund is one of the first to successfully appeal a citizenship rejection under Sweden's new longer residency requirements. Her arguments won't work for everyone, but the ruling could have wider implications if upheld.

articles.title: Centre-left holds on to power in Stockholm, Gothenburg and Malmö
articles.summary: The balance of power looks set to hold in the country's three largest municipalities, all of which are governed by centre-left coalitions.

articles.title: What you need to know about the local and regional elections in Gothenburg
articles.summary: The regional elections in Gothenburg and the surrounding region see the red-green coalitions which took power in 2022 defending their record on healthcare, traffic management, schools, and elderly care, as the right-wing parties try to limit further gains.

articles.title: Self-driving bus crashes with tram in Gothenburg on first day
articles.summary: A self-driving bus was involved in a crash with a tram on its first day carrying passengers in the Swedish city of Gothenburg.

articles.title: 'An international hub': These are the best districts for foreigners in Gothenburg
articles.summary: Majorna, the long-gentrified former working class district of central Gothenburg, and the adjoining Linné have been ranked the best district for foreigners in the city by readers of The Local, although many readers also rated Hisingen as a convenient and comfortable place to settle.

articles.title: What's that haze in the air in Gothenburg?
articles.summary: Swedish newspapers are reporting that for three days there's been a thick layer of smog covering the west coast city of Gothenburg.

articles.title: Gothenburg council withdraws monkey images after racism accusations
articles.summary: Social services in north-eastern Gothenburg were criticised for structural racism after using monkeys instead of humans in counselling material for children and young people in the area.

articles.title: Five reasons Sweden should move its capital to Gothenburg
articles.summary: Historically Stockholm was a natural choice for Sweden's capital. But times have changed. Here are the some of the reasons why Sweden should switch its political and business centre to Gothenburg, the gateway to Scandinavia.

articles.title: Which Swedish cities are most popular among young professionals?
articles.summary: A new study from Stockholm-based research company Future Place Leadership listed Gothenburg as the most attractive Swedish city to live and work in.

articles.title: 'Stay home' warning as Storm Louis blows roof off Gothenburg station
articles.summary: Police have warned people to stay inside as Storm Louis batters western Sweden, blowing parts of the roof off Gothenburg Central Station.

articles.title: Dead body found after fire at Gothenburg's Liseberg amusement park
articles.summary: One person has been found dead after a fire destroyed Liseberg's new water park Oceana, which had been set to open this summer.

articles.title: One man missing after fire inferno at Sweden's biggest amusement park
articles.summary: A man is missing after a fire broke out at the Liseberg amusement park in Gothenburg, with shocking images showing its newly built water park in flames.

articles.title: 'Unique' Viking graves change what we know about central Gothenburg
articles.summary: Swedish archaeologists have described two Viking graves as 'unique' after they were discovered in central Gothenburg, shedding new light on the history of Sweden’s second-largest city.

articles.title: Heartwarming story about Gothenburg's public library goes viral
articles.summary: What do you do if the library is officially closed but you manage to sneak in anyway? Borrow books, of course.

articles.title: TRAVEL: Number of daily trains between Oslo and Gothenburg to double
articles.summary: The number of daily train departures between the Norwegian capital of Oslo and the Swedish city of Gothenburg will double this winter, rail company Vy announced Thursday.

articles.title: How to have a cheap holiday in Sweden this summer
articles.summary: Things are looking better in the Swedish economy, but many households are still feeling the pinch. No matter the size of your budget, you don't have to miss out on all the fun this summer.

articles.title: Christmas in Sweden 2026: The best julbord in the Gothenburg area
articles.summary: Whether you're a Swedish Christmas newbie or a seasoned julbord connoisseur, here's The Local's selection of some of the best (often fishy) festive meals in the Gothenburg area. Feel free to share other tips in the comments!

articles.title: Why is 'everyone called Glenn' in Gothenburg?
articles.summary: We find out if everyone in Gothenburg is really called Glenn and where the old joke comes from.

articles.title: Moving to Gothenburg? The best areas and neighbourhoods to live in
articles.summary: Whether you're moving to Sweden’s second biggest city for the first time or are looking for another neighbourhood, The Local talks you through some of your best options.

articles.title: Five great day trips to do from Gothenburg
articles.summary: Gothenburg has a lively culture scene, plenty of green spaces and food and drink in abundance, but sometimes you just need to escape the city. The West Coast and nearby towns provide plenty of opportunities for a memorable day trip from Sweden's second city: here are five of our favourite destinations complete with insider tips.

articles.title: The story of the biggest fire disaster in Swedish history
articles.summary: At a Halloween party in Gothenburg in 1998, a fire started by four youths led to one of the deadliest disasters of modern Swedish history. Sixty-three young people lost their lives and many more were injured.
